paras: The Russellville depot platform fight was a clash in Russellville, Arkansas, in August 1900, in which a group of white boys drove some Black people off the railroad depot platform and followed them, and the Black men turned on them with knives. Will Davenport was fatally injured and Clarence Montgomery, a white man, was badly cut. The episode is known only from one short paragraph that circulated through Arkansas weeklies in the last week of August.

According to the paragraph, "a difficulty occurred between some negroes and white boys at Russellville" at the depot. The white boys made the Black people leave the depot platform and then followed them some distance. At that point, the report said, "the negroes then turned on the whites and began to use their knives." Will Davenport suffered what the item called a "fatal injury," and Clarence Montgomery, described as white, "was also badly cut."

The paragraph does not give Davenport's race, though the word "also" places him among the whites, and it does not state outright that he died. None of the Black participants is named, no injuries to them are reported, and the date of the fight is not given.
No report of arrests, an inquest or any prosecution appears in the coverage.

The Forrest City Times printed the item on August 24 under the headline "White Boys and Negroes Fight," the earliest printing found. The same words ran in the Van Buren Press on August 25, the Malvern Times-Journal on August 29 and the Paris Express on August 30. The De Queen Bee carried it on August 31 inside an "Arkansas State News" column. The Conway Log Cabin ran it on August 28 as "Whites and Blacks Fight."

Every version was the same unsigned item, printed without comment, and it stated plainly that the white boys had started the trouble by driving the Black people from the platform. No Black newspaper coverage of the fight was found.
